title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 20-21 of the manuscript): 'the question of full faithfulness' for the birational anabelian functor. K and K' are finitely generated fields over Q. Their algebraic closures of Q inside them, k and k', are identified and embedded in a fixed Q-bar, so k = k'. The absolute Galois groups then sit in extensions 1 -> pi_K -> E_K -> Gamma -> 1 and 1 -> pi_{K'} -> E_{K'} -> Gamma -> 1, with Gamma = Gal(Q-bar/k) and pi_K the geometric part Gal(K-bar/K.Q-bar).

The question is whether every homomorphism pi_{K'} -> pi_K that commutes with Gamma comes from a field embedding. On this page Grothendieck says that answering it requires a way to reconstruct K, K' from the outer profinite groups pi_K, pi_{K'} together with their outer Gamma-action. He guesses that 'Theorem 3 of the preceding §' could be the key. That theorem concerns (in a way only partly legible) P^1_K suitably punctured. This presumably means reconstruction via hyperbolic curves P^1 minus points, i.e. using fibrations of K by such curves.

The heuristic is that arbitrary outer homomorphisms pi_{K'-bar} -> pi_{K-bar} have no geometric meaning. The Gamma-action is 'so draconian' that the only Gamma-equivariant outer homomorphisms should be geometric, i.e. induced by field embeddings. This needs an arithmetic base, Q or equivalently a finitely generated field over Q, not an arbitrary field such as an algebraically closed one.

He then imposes a restriction: one must only consider homomorphisms pi_{K'} -> pi_K with open image. The counterexample (continued on p. 21) is K' = k, pi_{K'} = 1, which would yield a nonexistent map K -> k. On p. 21 he adds an 'admissibility' condition (trivial centralizers of images of open subgroups). He observes that the truly relevant objects are maps of extensions E_{K'} -> E_K. In the case K' = k these are sections of E_K over Gamma, which is the section conjecture in germ. He then formulates the question-conjecture in topos language: morphisms B_{K'} -> B_K over B_Q.

In modern terms this is the Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture over finitely generated fields: Isom/Hom_open^{out}(G_{K'}, G_K) over G_Q corresponds to embeddings K -> K'. The direction of the field maps should be noted; see the errors list.
errors: The direction of the field homomorphism is used inconsistently between pages. On p. 20, Pi_{K'} -> Pi_K is said to come from 'K' -> K' and later from 'K -> K''. Contravariance of Galois groups requires an embedding K -> K' (up to purely inseparable issues, irrelevant in char 0) to induce G_{K'} -> G_K. The p. 21 example (pi_{K'} trivial giving a 'hom K -> k') confirms that K -> K' is the intended direction.

Not an error, but the qualifier matters: without the open-image (or admissibility) hypothesis the statement is false, as he himself notes. In the modern theorems (Pop; Mochizuki 1999) only open homomorphisms are treated.

ideas.what: Gamma-equivariant outer homomorphisms between geometric fundamental groups of function fields over a finitely generated field should all be geometric (come from field embeddings): full faithfulness of the birational anabelian functor
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian conjecture (Hom-form) over finitely generated fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, Letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); proved by Pop (Isom form, 1994), Mochizuki (Hom form for sub-p-adic fields, 1999); also Neukirch-Uchida in dimension 0
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

ideas.what: Necessity of an arithmetic base field (finitely generated over Q), not an arbitrary field
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian geometry requires arithmetic ground fields (finitely generated / sub-p-adic)

ideas.what: Restriction to homomorphisms with open image (and trivial-centralizer 'admissibility') to exclude trivial counterexamples
ideas.modern_name: Open homomorphisms in the Hom-form anabelian theorems

ideas.what: Reconstruction of K from the outer Gamma-action, keyed to a theorem about suitably punctured P^1_K
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of birational anabelian statements to hyperbolic curves / P^1 minus points (fibration method)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programme); realized differently by Pop, Mochizuki

missed.claim: This early, pre-Esquisse formulation shows that the open-image restriction for the Hom-form birational conjecture was identified by Grothendieck around 1981, together with the role of punctured P^1_K as the intended reconstruction key. This is a historical precision on the genesis rather than a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: Encore faut-il se borner aux hom pi_{K'} -> pi_K dont on décrète d'avance que l'image soit ouverte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: the Hom-form with open image is usually attributed in its precise form to Mochizuki 1999. Grothendieck's own notes already isolate this hypothesis.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a heuristic, programmatic discussion of the birational anabelian conjecture that is well known from the Letter to Faltings and the Esquisse. The only mildly notable details are the explicit open-image restriction and the hope that a theorem on punctured P^1_K gives the reconstruction.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'profinis' is an interlinear insertion above 'extérieurs', so read 'des groupes profinis extérieurs avec opération de Gamma dessus'.
The parenthesis '(où [?] W[?] lignée[?] notamment à P^1_K ...)' is poorly read. It is probably '(appliqué notamment à P^1_K convenablement troué ...)' or similar; uncertain.
In 'des homomorphismes extérieurs quelconques pi_{K'-bar} -> pi_{K-bar}' the image shows bars over K' and K. Later on the page it reads 'pi_{K'} -> pi_K' without bars.
'ou, ce qui revient manifestement au même, un corps de type fini sur Q' — the image wording is closer to 'une extension de type fini de Q' as transcribed; acceptable.
